hints: Focus on what happens when each Period 3 oxide and chloride meets water, acidic, alkaline or no reaction.
Remember that magnesium oxide is sparingly soluble to give Mg(OH)2, while aluminium chloride and the chlorides of Si and P hydrolyse to give acidic solutions.
Compare a mixture that can supply OH- ions with mixtures that only supply H+ ions, and pick the one that must be the most alkaline.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Period 3 trend in pH**

Think left to right across Period 3. Oxides go from basic to amphoteric to acidic. Chlorides go from neutral to acidic, and the acidity gets stronger to the right.

General idea:
$$\text{basic oxide} \rightarrow \text{pH} > 7, \quad \text{acidic hydrolysis} \rightarrow \text{pH} < 7$$

**Check the magnesium mixture**

Magnesium oxide is a basic oxide. It reacts sparingly with water to form magnesium hydroxide, a weak alkali.

$$\text{MgO(s) + H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$$ 
Magnesium chloride dissolves to give $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ with essentially neutral solution, about pH 6 to 7. So overall the mixture is alkaline, around pH 9.

**Check the other three mixtures**

Aluminium oxide, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, is insoluble and does nothing, but aluminium chloride hydrolyses strongly acidic:
$$\text{[Al(H}_2\text{O)}_6\text{]}^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{[Al(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{(OH)]}^{2+} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$
This gives pH about 3. Phosphorus oxides ($\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$) and phosphorus chlorides ($\text{PCl}_3$, $\text{PCl}_5$) both hydrolyse to give strong acid mixtures including $\text{HCl}$ and phosphoric acid, pH 1 to 2. Silicon dioxide, $\text{SiO}_2$, is insoluble, but silicon tetrachloride hydrolyses completely:
$$\text{SiCl}_4\text{(l) + 2H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2\text{(s) + 4HCl(aq)}$$ 
This is also strongly acidic.

**Conclude the highest pH**

Only the magnesium mixture contains a source of $\text{OH}^-$ ions with no strong acid produced. All the others contain a chloride that generates $\text{H}^+$ ions.

So the magnesium oxide plus magnesium chloride solution is the only alkaline one, and must have the highest pH.

options.A: Aluminium oxide is insoluble and has no effect on pH, but aluminium chloride undergoes acidic hydrolysis to form $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ with pH around 3. The solution is acidic, so it cannot be the highest pH.
options.B: Magnesium oxide reacts to give sparingly soluble Mg(OH)2, which is alkaline (pH about 9). Magnesium chloride is approximately neutral and does not cancel this alkalinity. This is the only alkaline mixture, so it has the highest pH.
options.C: Both phosphorus oxides and phosphorus chlorides hydrolyse to give very acidic solutions containing phosphoric acid and HCl, with pH 1 to 2. This is strongly acidic, the opposite of highest pH.
options.D: Silicon dioxide is insoluble and unreactive with water, but SiCl4 hydrolyses completely to give 4 moles of HCl per mole. The resulting solution is strongly acidic (pH about 1 to 2), so it is much lower than the magnesium mixture.
